Subject: Marketplace commitment bands and annual fee ceiling — restructure proposal

Hi all,

Were re-evaluating our marketplace listing economics ahead of next years budgeting cycle and I wanted to get initial alignment with each partner on a potential restructure. Attached is a first-pass workbook (RI_Marketplace_Commitment_Bands_v1.xlsx) that models tiered commitment bands and an annual fee ceiling rather than the current flat percentage model.

High-level asks:
- Can each of you confirm whether your partner programs have the flexibility to convert to a banded commit model (0-250k / 250-1M / 1M+) with an explicit annual fee cap?
- For AWS and GCP, any standard language we should expect in term sheets for ceilings or revenue smoothing?
- Can we schedule a 30m sync next week to walk the workbook and surface operational impacts (invoicing, attribution, co-sell credits)?

Why this matters: the banded approach gives us predictability for forecast and creates a clear scale advantage for customers as they grow—should reduce churn and make committed spend easier to guarantee to partners.

Im copying finance and partnerships so we can iterate quickly. Proposed times: Tue 10/13 10:00 PT or Wed 10/14 08:00 PT.

Thanks,
Irene
Irene Choi
Head of Partnerships, Redwood Inference

Irene,

Thanks for the workbook — we can definitely look at banded commitments. A few quick notes from the AWS Partner Programs side:
- We typically allow tiered CPAs (commitment + rebate) but annual ceilings are evaluated case-by-case. The attached AWS_term_summary_2026-10.pdf has examples weve agreed with other ISVs.
- Any ceiling language usually ties to attribution and billing cadence; well need to confirm how Redwood reports marketplace ARR vs direct billing.
- Wed like to see a projected cohort of 6-12 months of usage by band to assess risk.

Im available Tue 10/13 10:00 PT for a call. Can you add an operations contact for invoicing details?

Best,
Elena

Irene + team,

Helpful starter — a couple of internal considerations from finance before we lock anything down:
- We need a target blended take-rate (net of credits) across small / mid / enterprise bands. My back-of-envelope suggests wed need to keep blended unit economics within 1.5x current for FY27 to hit margin targets.
- Any ceiling needs an explicit mechanism for clawback or reconciliation if attribution drops below a threshold (this is non-negotiable for our FP&A team).
- If partners cant agree to ceilings, consider a hybrid: soft ceilings with quarterly true-ups plus a performance corridor.

Related: HubSpot deal DEAL-8392 (high probability) would be the first customer to move to the banded model; Ill attach an ARR cohort in the workspace for a reference model.

If we take a negotiating approach, Id prioritize: (1) AWS (largest revenue), (2) Azure (lowest friction), (3) GCP (strategic co-sell).

Marcus

Team,

I remodeled the bands in the attached GCP_fee_table_draft.csv with three alternatives: conservative, baseline, and aggressive. Key suggestions:
- Conservative: lower ceiling, tighter clawbacks — minimizes Redwoods downside but reduces partner uplift potential.
- Baseline: moves to the banded model with a 12% blended take-rate target and a 10% contingency true-up quarterly.
- Aggressive: higher customer discounts but larger co-sell incentives; split marketing funds to front-load 60% in Q1.

Numbers (baseline example):
- Band A (0-250k): 8.5% take + $3k fixed annual platform fee cap
- Band B (250k-1M): 10% take + $15k cap
- Band C (1M+): 7% take + $50k cap

Requests: please review the attachments and signal objections by EOD Tue 10/13 so we can present consolidated asks to AWS/GCP/Azure on our call. Ill also add the cohort data Marcus mentioned.

Karthik
Head of Finance Planning & Strategy, Redwood Inference

- External asks: each marketplace team to confirm legal language for an annual ceiling, attribution requirements, and invoicing cadence.
- Primary focus: AWS first, then Azure, then GCP.

Next steps:
